full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts for the disposal of the appeal, in short, are that the appellants instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration of their title in the suit covering an area of 1.20 acres of C.S. Plot No. 1 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 53 of Mouza Kakrail., Police Station Ramna, (former Keranigonj) Dhaka alleging, inter alia, that the suit land along with other lands measuring 48.90 acres of said Plot and Khatian corresponding to S.A. Plot No.64 and S.A. Khatian No. 26 originally belonged to Bhawal Zaminder Rajkumer Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury who settled the suit land to Ashraf Ali Kazi, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs executing a pattannama on 05.02.1905. Said Ashraf Ali Kazi took over possession of the suit land and paid rent to the Zaminder. In C.S. operation, the suit land along with other lands of the disputed jam, was recorded in the name of Public Works Department under Bharat Samrat. Against the said record of right Ashraf Ali Kazi filed objection to get the same corrected and got an order on 24.05.1925. In S.A. operation the same was again recorded in the name of Public Works Department. On 12.01.1992, the plaintiffs discovered the pattannama, rent receipts and mutated C.S. Khatian in an old box in their house. On 08.03.1992, they collected the certified copies of the S.A. and C.S. Khatians and confirmed about the erroneous preparation of S.A. record of right. Thereafter, they filed this suit. 

 3. The defendant-respondents contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the that the suit land along with other lands covering 48.90 acres originally belonged to Public Works Department under Bharat Samrat. Accordingly, the same was recorded in C.S. Plot No. 1 and khatian No. 53. Subsequently the Deputy. Commissioner, Dhaka took over possession of the suit land. The story of settlement of the plaintiffs from Bhawal Rajkumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury is false and the document produced by the plaintiffs are forged and fabricated. The C.S. Khatian had not been corrected at the instance of the plaintiffs' predecessor. The corrected Khatian produced by the plaintiffs is forged. The Government has been possessing the suit land. The Government started to construct buildings in the suit land for residential purpose of higher Government Officials. The S.A. record of right was duly prepared in the name of the Government. The suit should be dismissed. 

 6. Mr. A.F. Hasan Arif, the senior Counsel 'appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiff-appellants got the suit land by way of settlement in the year 1905 and produced more than 30 years old pattannama (exhibit-1) . The plaintiffs paid rents to the Zaminder vide Exhibit-2 series and they got the C.S. Khatian corrected vide exhibit-3 series and had been possessing the suit land more than 87 years. The third Judge of the High Court Division has committed an error of law in disbelieving the pattannama, corrected C.S. Khatian and rent receipts. He submits that the findings of the third Judge of the High Court Division regarding authenticity of exhibit-1 made in an old British Indian Stamp of 1905, and the rent receipts (exhib-it-2 series), the corrected C.S. Khatian (exhibit 3 series) and exhibit-4, the volume book of Government containing C.S. Khatian are erroneous. He further submits that since price of the land was Tk. 15/- only as it appears in the pattannama, the same was not required to he registered under section 17 of the Registration Act. 

 7. Mr. Goutom Kumar, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that the High Court Division on vivid discussions on the materials on record came to the conclusion that the pattannama, rent receipts of the Zamindar and corrected C.S. Khatian are forged and fabricated documents. He submits that Mr. Justice Md. Abdur Rashid rightly directed to prosecute the plaintiff-appellants initiating proceeding under Section 476 read with 195 (1) (c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, on allegation of forging those documents. He submits that the plaintiffs had no title-and possession in the suit land. The Government, constructing the buildings in the suit land; has been possessing the same. The instant suit was not at all maintainable without the prayer for recovery of khas possession. 

 10. Submission of Mr. Arif is that since the Ext. 1 Pattannama is an old document of more than 30 years and had been produced from proper custody, the court would presume that the signature and every other part of Ext.1 is that person's hand writing and, the same had been duly executed by the person by whom it purports to be executed as per provision of Section 90 of the Evidence Act. The spirit of section 90 of the Evidence Act is that if private documents not less than thirty years old are produced from proper custody and are on their face free from suspicion, the court may presume at they w have been signed or written by the persons whose signatures they bear or in whose hand writing they purport to he, that they have been duly attested and executed, if they purport so to he Section 90 only lays down that the court may presume that document purporting to be 30 years old are genuine. That it must not presume them to be so. Supreme Court of India in the case of Sri Lakhi Baruah Vs. Sri Padma Kanta Kalita reported in AIR 1996 SC 1253 observed that Section 90 of the Evidence Act is founded on necessity and convenience because it is extremely difficult and sometimes not possible to lead evidence to prove handwriting, signature or execution of old documents after lapse of 30 years. In order to obviate such difficulties or improbabilities to prove execution of an old documents section 30 has been incorporated in the Evidence Act, which does away with the strict rule of proof of private documents. Presumption of genuineness may he raised if the document in question is produced from proper custody. It is, however, the discretion of the Court to accept the presumption flowing from Section. The presumption is permissive and accordance no the circumstances of each case the court may or may not raise it. That is, such presumption discretionary and so where a document is suspicious on the face of it or mutilated, the court may refuse to make presumption. It is not obligatory on a court to raise the presumption. The language being "may" when the person who has been examined as P.W.2 to prove the Ext.1 himself has said “১নং প্রদর্শনী পড়তে পারবো না"; then why the court will rely upon such document .At the time of making exhibit the defendant raised objection saving, লেখা অষ্পষ্ট ও ছেড়া প্রঃ ১টি। In such circumstances, the provision of section 90 ought to be applied with more care and great caution because nothing can he more easy than, for an unscrupulous ours person, who is wrongfully in possession and wants to make out a title to it to forge such document in his favour more than 30 years old and produce it as the proper custodian relieving himself of the necessity of proving its execution. The Ext. 1 patina must not be presumed to he genuine merely from its being ancient. Some other evidence were required to be given of the early existence and publicity of Ext. 1 . Neither C. S. khatian nor S. A. khatian had been prepared on the basis of Ext. 1. 

 11. In order to show the existence and publicity of Ext.1 or in other words to prove the story of their settlement dated 11.02.1905 and rebut the presumption under Section 103. B of the Bengal Tenancy Act, which is available in favour of the Government since C.S. record of right was prepared in favour of the Government ( Ext. A), the plaintiffs produced Ext .2 series, the Zamindari dakhilas and alleged corrected khatian Ext. 3 series. It is the claim of the plaintiffs that against C.S. Khatian their predecessor Ashraf Ali Kazi filed Objection Case No. 327H/1932 and got his name corrected in the Zamindery Sherista and obtained certified copies of the corrected Khatian from Zamindery sherist- Correction of the entry in Khatian filing objection in the Zamindery Sherista is totally illegal. As per provision of Section 108A of the Bengal Tenancy Act, which was transferred as section 115B, by the Bengal Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1928, only the Revenue Officer specially empowered by the Government on application or of his own motion, within two years (earlier time limit was for 12 months) from the date of certificate of the final publication of the record of right under sub-section (2) of Section 103A, correct any entry in such record of rights which he was satisfied had been made owing to a bonafide mistake. That is, Revenue Officer was legally authorized to correct the Khatian nobody else. The concerned volume regarding P.S. Khatian was called for to ascertain the authenticity of Ext. 3 series which was marked as Ext. 4 . T. Islam, J examined Ext. 3 series, the corrected Khatian produced by the plaintiffs and relevant volume book of C.S. khatian Ext. 4 thoroughly. Such examination, as it appears from his observation that the same was made most carefully which is praise-worthy. 

 "I have gone through Ext. 4, which is the volume of Mouza 282 Kakrail produced before the trial court. In C.S. Khatian Nos. 1, 2, 9-10, 13, 24, 53 and 55 as contained in Ext. 4, on the top of the front page at the left hand side under the heading  উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words "ভারত সম্রাট" have been printed and out of the above Khatian at the right hand side of the Khatian Nos. 1, 2, 9-10, 13-24 under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে বিস্তারিত দখল the names of different persons were printed and in the remaining C.S. Khatian Nos. 53 and 57, under this very heading at right hands side, public works Department and District Board respectively, both on behalf of Bharat Samrat were printed. In C.S. Khatian Nos. 3, 4, 5, 6 and 17 as contained in Ext. 4 similarly under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the word পত্তন রাজেন্দ্র নারায়ণ রায় ৩নং কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ড were printed and out of the above khatian under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল of C.S. Khatian Nos.  4,5 and 6 the names of different persons were printed and in C.S. Khatian Nos. 3 and 7 only, and this heading " কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ডস’"Were printed. 

 In C.S. Khatian Nos. 31-32, 33Ka, 34-35, 39-40, 43, 46-47 and 47Ka as contained in Ext. 4 under the heading উপরিস্তস্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words পত্তনী কালীন নারায়ন রায় ৩০নং দখল কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ডস were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of different persons were printed and in C.S. Khatian No. 8, as contained in Ext. 4 under the heading উপরিস্থ স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words মিরস জামাল, ৭নং রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ড were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of Sheikh Abdul was printed. 

 In C.S. Khatian Nos. 30, 51Ka and 51 Kha as contained in Ext. 4, under the heading অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the words সিকিম তালুক রামকৃষ্ণ দত্ত were printed and out of the above Khatians, in C.S. Khatian No. 30 under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the words কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ডস were printed and in Khatian No. 51 Ka and 51 Kha under the above heading of অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the names of other persons were printed. 

 In C.S. Khatian No. 25-27 and 51 as contained in Ext. 4 under the heading উপরিসত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words and also the names of 13 co-sharers of the Zamindari were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of different persons were printed. 

 Thus in the Khatians mentioned above on the front page on the top at left hand side under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/ পরিচয়ে the names of Zamindars were printed and at the right hand side under the heading অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of tenants/riots were printed and at the over leafs of some of the above Khatians, the names of the possessors were printed. 

 Regarding C.S. Khatian No. 53 as contains in Ext. 4, as it appears at left hand side under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words ভারত সম্রাট were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/ অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of Public Works Department on behalf of Bharat Samrat, have been printed and it is only at the over leaf, Kumar Rabindra Narayan himself was shown as mere possessors of 48.90 acres of land in C.S. Plot No. 1 as stated earlier, in C.S. Khatian Nos. 3-7, 8, 30, 31, 32, 32 Ka 33, 34, 39; 40, 43,47, 51Ka and 51 Kha of Ext. 4 in most of the cases the Court of words of the heirs of Kumar Rabindra Narayan have been shown as Zamindars and in few cases the above court of words have been shown ryot under the heading" অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল and is none of the above Khatians Kumar Rabindra Narayan himself was not shown as Zamindar or tenant. It thus appears that on 23.04.1917, when the above C.S. Khatian were finally published, Kumar Rabindra Narayan ceased hold any interest in any of the above Khatians and instead the court of wards of his heirs were shown as Zamindar and tenants. 

 Accordingly how in C.S. Khatian No. 53 as contained in Ext. 4 Kumar Rabindra Narayan could be shown as possessor and like wise how in Ext. 3 also Kumar Rabindra Narayan himself could be shown as Zamindar." 

 14. Mr. Arif failed to satisfy this court making any submission to discard aforesaid findings referring any material on record. The aforesaid findings arrived at by the last court of facts are based evidence. Since Kumer Rabindra Narayon was neither landlord nor tenant in the land recorded in Khatian No. 53 and plot No. 1 no one, claiming himself as manager of Kumer Rabindra Narayon Chowdhury, had any authority to settle the same on his behalf. He was not a person immediately under whom the tenant holds and no tenancy had been established pursuant to Ext. 1 in re sport of the suit land. 

 16. The plaintiffs stated that their predecessor Ashraf Ali Kazi died sometime in 1948. It has also been stated in the plaint that in 1992 the plaintiffs allegedly got the papers produced in the Court in an old box. The plaintiffs did not produce any materials in support of their claim to deal with the property, at least, from 1948 to 1992. They did not take any step to record their names in the khatian and to pay rent to the Government. It is totally unacceptable proposition' that one, who is allegedly in possession in the land and structure thereon within Dhaka City Corporation, would not take any step to record/ mutate his name in the khatian, pay rent, municipal taxes, WASA, Gas bills etc.
